# Ratanacaṅkamanakaṇḍa (Bv 1)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ratanacaṅkamanakaṇḍa* ("The Jewel-walk" or "Section on the Jewel Walk") constitutes the introductory chapter (Bv 1) of the *Buddhavaṁsa* [Lim Hwee San 2009; SuttaCentral]. In this chapter, the Buddha displays his supranormal power by creating a walkway adorned with jewels [Lim Hwee San 2009]. Sāriputta then questions the Buddha about the nature of his original resolve (*abhinīhāra*) for awakening (*kīdiso te mahāvīra, abhinīhāro naruttama*), a query that frames the Buddha's exposition of the lives of the previous twenty-four Buddhas that forms the rest of the work [Lim Hwee San 2009]. The chapter also includes poetic descriptions of disciples, such as verse 1.58 portraying Moggallāna's skin as having the dark blue hue of a rain cloud or a blue lotus (*nīluppala*) [Sujato 2011].

SuttaCentral records two translations of the text in two languages and notes an association with the *Upacālāsutta* (SN 5.7) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text-reuse matches from DharmaNexus document extensive Pali-internal reuse across commentarial literature, most substantially in the *Buddhavaṁsa-aṭṭhakathā* (72 matches, such as §§24.1–38.4), as well as the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (notably §§75.1–79.4) and the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§§68.1–68.4) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus indicate verse and phrasing matches in Tibetan Mahāyāna sūtras, including the *Samādhirāja-sūtra* (D0127), the *Ratnākara-sūtra* (D0124), and the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* (D0557) [DharmaNexus].
